facts.fact: The Job context menu has the entry 'Update Tools from Library' with the icon CAM_UpdateDocumentTools.svg. The entry does the check for that one Job only.
When the manual check finds no changed tool, a message box shows with the title 'Update Tools from Library' and the text 'This job has no tool updates available.'

The check at document load occurs only when the preference ToolUpdateOnLoad is on. It occurs one time for each load of a document, after restore and recompute are complete, and it examines all Jobs of the document. The dialog shows only when a minimum of one Job has a changed tool; if not, nothing shows.

The dialog title is 'Tool Updates Available'. The two entry points (document load and Job context menu) use the same dialog. The preference does not prevent the manual check from the Job context menu.

The introduction text of the dialog is: "'{}' has tools that differ from the library (newer presets, changed dimensions - e.g. a regrind - or both). Updating replaces the whole tool with the current library version and recomputes the document - expand a row to review before applying." The placeholder is the document label at load and the Job label for the manual check.

The dialog table has one row for each changed tool and five columns: a checkbox column without header text, 'Job', 'Tool #', 'Tool' and 'Changes'. 'Tool #' is the ToolNumber of the Tool Controller and 'Tool' is the Label of the embedded Tool Bit. Rows are in the sequence of Job label, then tool number.
Each row checkbox is checked by default. A checkbox in the table header (tooltip 'Select all') checks or clears all rows and shows a partial state when only some rows are checked.
The dialog buttons are 'Update' and the standard Cancel button. Cancel is the default button. 'Update' is disabled when no row is checked. Cancel changes nothing.

The 'Changes' cell shows 'Presets', 'Geometry' or 'Presets, Geometry'. Only a row with geometry changes is a tree that expands. The tree has one line 'Presets' when presets differ and one line '<property label>: <old value> → <new value>' for each changed property. A row with only preset changes is plain text and does not expand.
The old and new values in the Changes tree are shown in the Units (Metric or Imperial) of the library Tool Bit, not of the embedded Tool Bit.

An embedded Tool Bit is compared only with the Tool Bit in the local library store that has the same ToolBitID. A Tool Bit with no ToolBitID, or with a ToolBitID that is not in the library, is ignored and is not in the dialog. There is no match by label or by other values.

A tool is in the dialog only when its Presets differ from the library, or a property of the 'Shape' property group that the two objects have differs, or both. A property that only one of the two has is not compared. If the ShapeType of the two differs, no geometry comparison is made.

facts.fact: An update always replaces the full Tool Bit: FreeCAD attaches a new full copy of the library Tool Bit to the document, sets the Tool property of the Tool Controller to the new object, and removes the old Tool Bit object from the document. There is no update of only presets or only geometry, and no merge of fields.

Because the old object is removed, all local edits of the embedded Tool Bit are lost on update: presets edited in the Job, Shape values, Units and other attributes get the library values. An update cannot be applied to a part of a tool.

The Camotics export writes, for each tool, the keys "units", "shape", "length", "diameter" and "description". "units" is "imperial" when the user unit schema shows the tool diameter in an imperial unit (in, ", thou, ft, '); if not, it is "metric". The decision is made for each tool from its diameter, and the Units property of the Tool Bit is not used.

In the Camotics export, "diameter" and "length" are bare numbers in inches when "units" is "imperial" and in millimetres when "units" is "metric". The length always uses the same unit as the diameter of that tool.

In the Camotics export, "diameter" and "length" are rounded to the number of decimals of the parameter Decimals in BaseApp/Preferences/Units (default 2 when the parameter is not set). The fixed Tool Bit precision of 3 or 4 decimals does not apply to this export.

The Camotics import reads the "units" key of each tool entry: "imperial" gives Diameter and Length in inches, "metric" gives millimetres. If the key is absent or has a different value, the import uses millimetres. The unit schema of the user and the Units Decimals preference do not change the import.

Points for the writers:
- Plan wording 'next free number': the default is the highest Tool Number of the Job plus 1 (F38), not the lowest unused number. Write 'the next tool number of the Job'.
- The request for a tool number does not always occur. It occurs always on a conflict (F39). For a tool without a library number it occurs only when the Toolbit Selector was opened by Add Toolbit…, the Tool Controller command or an operation panel; from the Tools tab of the Job editor the tool gets the next number without a prompt (F36). job/job.adoc is out of scope, but tools/add-toolbit.adoc must not say that the prompt always shows.
- The present tools/add-toolbit.adoc says that the Job editor uses a dialog 'Select Toolbit' and that only that dialog has 'All Tools'. This is no longer correct: all four entry points open the 'Toolbit Selector' with 'All Tools' (F34, F35).
- The present tools/toolbit-library.adoc says 'the library number becomes the Tool Controller's Tool Number'. This is now true only when no different tool of the Job has that number (F40).
- Tools are 'different' by ToolBitID (F42). Two copies of the same library Tool Bit in a Job are the same tool for the number rule.
- The warning 'Tool Number In Use' in F43 is the one of the Tool Controller editor (context CAM_ToolController). The same text in the Job tool table belongs to job/job.adoc and is not documented in this unit.
- Units and precision have three different rules; do not mix them: (1) saved Tool Bit values and ToolBit editor fields use the Units of the Tool Bit and 3 or 4 decimals, independent of the unit schema and of Units Decimals (F27, F29); (2) the Camotics export uses the unit schema of the user and Units Decimals, not the Units of the Tool Bit (F50 to F52); (3) the Camotics import uses only the "units" key of the file (F53). The LinuxCNC .tbl export in the present tools/toolbit-library.adoc was not changed by this unit.
- The present tools/toolbit.adoc says that Units is the 'unit system used to display the Tool Bit's parameters'. Units now also sets the unit and precision of the saved values (F27).
- The update dialog text says 'newer presets', but the code only tests that presets differ (F12). An embedded Tool Bit with local preset edits is listed as changed, and an update removes those edits (F14). This is the important point of goal 2.
- The verdict for 32278 names the page 'CAM preferences'; the group 'Tool Bit Shape Drawing' is on the 'GUI' page (F19). The brightness has an effect only on a dark theme, as its label says.
- Not written as facts, because the unit lists them as not documented: sortable columns of the presets table, the hidden sort combo for 'All Tools', the highlight between a dimension and its field, the list entry format, the 25.4 statement, and the job/job.adoc changes.
- STE conflict: interface strings such as 'Updating replaces the whole tool…' and 'Tool number {} is already used by {}.' are quoted as the source spells them and do not follow STE.
